A small nut had fallen into a channel which prevented the gear from moving. C. A huge plane was forced to crash land when its landing gear got stuck. D. They were amazed when they discovered what had caused the mechanical failure.
questions.questionHtml:
Give below are four jumbled sentences, select the option that gives their correct order.

A. Expert mechanics laboured over the plane for three hours.

B. A small nut had fallen into a channel which prevented the gear from moving.

C. A huge plane was forced to crash land when its landing gear got stuck.

D. They were amazed when they discovered what had caused the mechanical failure.
questions.solution:
Sentence C comes first as it explains the scenario set in the passage (plane that suffered the crash landing). Sentence A follows and mentions that the expert mechanics looked over it for three hours.

Sentence D comes next. 'They' in sentence D refers to 'expert mechanics' mentioned in A. It mentions that they were amazed at something.

What amazed them is mentioned in sentence B, and it is the concluding sentence.

So, the correct order is CADB.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

It can be filled with the adjective 'creative'. Filling the blank with 'creative' gives the meaning that dance is an art form which involves using original and unusual ideas.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank number 3.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank number 3.
questions.solution:
'Much of' is used with the noun/noun phrases which are uncountable in essence. 'Dance forms' is a countable noun phrase, so 'many' should be used instead.

'More' is used to draw comparisons between two entities, which is not the case here.

'Any of the dance forms' would imply any one dance form from among many, and hence it would be a singular subject, nut the verb 'trace' is plural. So, 'any' cannot fill the blank as well.

Filling the third blank with 'many' makes the sentence contextually and grammatically correct.

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank number 4.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank number 4.
questions.solution:
The sentence implies that various dance forms trace their roots to 'Natya Shastra' by Bharat Muni.

Filling the fourth blank with 'techniques' gives the meaning that various dance forms use these techniques mentioned in Natya Shastra.

Other options render the sentence meaningless contextually. 'Procedure' is a particular method for performing a task while technique is the practical aspects of a given art, occupation etc.So, as per the context, 'techniques' is most appropriate to fill the blank.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank number 5.
questions.questionHtml: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank number 5.
questions.solution:
Captured - take into one's possession or control by force.

Dispersed - go or cause to go in different directions.

Compiled - produce (a list or book) by assembling information collected from other sources.

Disbursed -pay out (money from a fund).

The sentence with the given blank implies that various dance forms trace their roots to 'Natya Shastra' by Bharat Muni.

Filling the fifth blank with 'compiled' gives the meaning that Bharat Muni worked on the text 'Natya Shastra' by collecting information from other sources.

Other options render the sentence meaningless contextually.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate meaning of the following idiom. Feast one's eyes on

questions.questionHtml:

questions.question: Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank. Can you arrange for the consignment delivered on Monday?
questions.questionHtml:
Select the most appropriate option to fill in the blank.

Can you arrange for the consignment delivered on Monday?
questions.solution:
'Consignment' is the receiver of the verb 'delivered'. So, the given sentence is in passive voice.

Here, the correct format would be: 'Object ('consignment') + to + be + V3 ('delivered').

So, 'to be' will fill the blank appropriately.

The correct sentence is: Can you arrange for the consignment to be delivered on Monday?

Hence, option (a) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate ANTONYM of the given word. Proclaim
questions.questionHtml:

Proclaim
questions.solution:

Conceal - not allowed to be seen; hide.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

Exhibit - publicly display (a work of art or item of interest) in an art gallery or museum or at a trade fair.

Evince - reveal the presence of (a quality or feeling); indicate.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice. She is looking after the old ladies with great affection.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in passive voice.

She is looking after the old ladies with great affection.

options.text: She is looked after with great affection by the old ladies.
options.html: She is looked after with great affection by the old ladies.

options.text: The old ladies are looked after with great affection.
options.html: The old ladies are looked after with great affection.

options.text: The old ladies were looked after with great affection.
options.html: The old ladies were looked after with great affection.

options.text: The old ladies are being looked after with great affection.
options.html: The old ladies are being looked after with great affection.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Active Voice is changed into the object of the Passive Voice. Also, the object of the Active Voice is changed into the subject of the Passive Voice.

The usage of a "to be" form of verb is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Active to Passive.

In Passive Voice, the preposition "by" is used before the object. However, it is optional in some cases.

The Active voice in this question is in Present Continuous. Thus, the Passive voice will also be in Present Continuous.

The format of Active voice is: Subject + am/is/are + V1 + ing + Object.

Thus, in Passive voice, the format will be: Object of the active voice (Subjective case) + am/is/are + being + V3 + by + Subject of the active voice (Objective case).

For example:

Arnab is typing a document. (Active Voice)

A document is being typed by Arnab. (Passive Voice)

The options except (d) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (d): The old ladies are being looked after with great affection.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. Shall / we go / for walking / in the park?
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

Shall / we go / for walking / in the park?
questions.solution:
'For + V4 (-ing form of verb)' is used to mention a purpose for certain action ['go' in this sentence]. But, we don't use for + -ing to express our purpose or intention.

For example: We're going to Lisbon to visit my aunt. 'For visiting' would be inappropriate here.

Here, 'go for a walk' would be an appropriate phrase.

The correct sentence is: Shall we go for a walk in the park?

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error, select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. Vivek should be excited / on the promotion / he's got.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been divided into parts. One of them may contain an error, select the part that contains the error from the given options. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Vivek should be excited / on the promotion / he's got.
questions.solution:
When the verb 'excited' is followed by the noun depicting the source of excitement for the person ['promotion' in the given sentence'], then preposition 'about' is used with 'excited'. So, 'on' should be replaced with 'about'.

The correct sentence is: Vivek should be excited about the promotion he's got.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

The given sentence is error-free.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. I do not / like to read / these kind / of novels.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into four segments. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error.

I do not / like to read / these kind / of novels.
questions.solution:
The determiner 'these' is plural in form. So, it will be followed by the plural noun 'kinds', and not singular noun 'kind'.

So, the error is in the part in option (c).

The correct sentence is: I do not like to read these kinds of novels.

Hence, option (c) is the answer.

questions.question: The following sentence has been split into segments. One of them may contain an error. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer. Among you and me / she is quite rude / to the boy.
questions.questionHtml:
The following sentence has been split into segments. One of them may contain an error. Identify the segment that contains a grammatical error. If you don't find any error, mark 'No error' as your answer.

Among you and me / she is quite rude / to the boy.
questions.solution:
'Among' is used when there are more than two persons involved.

Here, only two persons are involved, so the preposition 'between' will be used in the sentence.

The correct sentence is: Between you and me, she is quite rude to the boy.

Hence, option (d) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed select 'No improvement'. You are so far the bright student in the class.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that will improve the underlined part of the given sentence. In case no improvement is needed select 'No improvement'.

You are so far the bright student in the class.
questions.solution:
'By far' means 'by a large amount; by a large degree'.

'So far' means 'until this point in time; until now'.

In the given context, 'so far' does not fit in the sentence as it would imply that the subject has been bright till present only, which the sentence does not intend to imply.

Replacing 'so far the bright' with 'by far the brightest' will imply that the subject is bright enough, to a great degree than all other students in the class.

The correct sentence is: You are by far the brightest student in the class.

Hence, option (b) is the answer.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice. Tall promises were being made by each promoter.
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in active voice.

Tall promises were being made by each promoter.

options.text: Each promoter has been making tall promises.
options.html: Each promoter has been making tall promises.

options.text: Each promoter was making tall promises.
options.html: Each promoter was making tall promises.

options.text: Each promoter has made tall promises.
options.html: Each promoter has made tall promises.

questions.solution:
The subject of the Passive Voice is changed into the object of the Active Voice. Also, the object of the Passive Voice is changed into the subject of the Active Voice.

The removal of the "to be" verb and the preposition 'by' is necessary while changing the voice of the sentence from Passive to Active.

The Passive voice in this question is in Past Continuous. Thus, the Active voice will also be in Past Continuous.

In Passive voice, the format is: Object of the Active voice (Subjective case) + was/were + being + V3 + by + Subject of the Active voice (Objective case).

Thus, the format of Active voice is: Subject + was/were + V1 + ing + Object.

For example:

Math was being practised by Amit. (Passive Voice)

Amit was practising Math. (Active Voice)

The options except (b) don't follow the correct grammatical format of the Passive Voice.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (b): Each promoter was making tall promises.

questions.question: Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech. He said to me, "Do you own this beautiful car?"
questions.questionHtml:
Select the option that expresses the given sentence in indirect speech.

He said to me, "Do you own this beautiful car?"

options.text: He asked me that if you owned this beautiful car.
options.html: He asked me that if you owned this beautiful car.

options.text: He asked me did I owned that beautiful car.
options.html: He asked me did I owned that beautiful car.

options.text: He asked me if I owned that beautiful car.
options.html: He asked me if I owned that beautiful car.

options.text: He asked to me if you own that beautiful car.
options.html: He asked to me if you own that beautiful car.

questions.solution:
In the case of Interrogative sentences like this, "said" in Direct Speech is changed into "enquired (of)", "wanted to know", "asked", etc.

In Indirect speech, the verb is always placed after the subject, unlike in Direct Speech.

If there is a question in Direct Speech whose answer can come as "Yes" or "No" in the Indirect Speech, we should use the conjunctions "if" or "whether".

For example:

Ravi said to me, "Is she studying?" (Direct Speech)

Ravi asked me if she was studying. (Indirect Speech)

Also, the sentence in the Direct Speech is in the Simple Present tense. So, the tense in the Indirect Speech should be in the Simple Past tense.

The following things in the sentence should change when changed from Direct speech to Indirect Speech:

'Said to' will be changed to 'asked'.

'Do you' will be changed to 'if I'.

'Own' will be changed to 'owned'.

'This' will be changed to 'that'.

Therefore, the correct answer is option (c):He asked me if I owned that beautiful car.
